title: Goat Feed Station Queue Time
dataSources: Hive metrics (`flowhive:reading`), egg counter events (`eggcounter:event`), goat RFID visits (`goattag:scan`), goat watering and feed logs (`goatcare:event`), and compost readings (`compost:reading`).
app: Smallholding and backyard telemetry from Flow Hive scales, chicken coop counters, RFID goat tags, compost thermometers, and camera-driven chore logs sent to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=goatcare:event
| search event_type="feed_queue" queue_sec=*
| stats avg(queue_sec) as avg_queue_sec perc90(queue_sec) as p90_queue_sec count as samples by station_id
| sort 0 - avg_queue_sec
description: Measures goat feed-station waiting time by feed station. Runs scheduled SPL against `index=personal` to surface **Goat Feed Station Queue Time** so you can spot drift before it becomes a habit.
value: Queue time shows whether one station is becoming a bottleneck or bullying hotspot.
implementation: Send the relevant duration field for goat feed-station waiting time to `index=personal` and review both average and p90 latency instead of relying on single examples.
visualization: Table of average and p90 goat feed-station waiting time.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Homestead, Bees & Livestock — typical feeds: Beehive telemetry (`beehive:reading`), coop door (`chickencoop:door`), egg counts (`egg:count`), livestock tags (`livestock:tag`), feed level (`feed:level`), pasture sensors (`pasture:sensor`), trail .
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `goatcare:event`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=goatcare:event`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Homestead sensors — connected beehive scale/temperature/sound, automatic chicken-coop door, egg counter, livestock GPS/health tags, feed-silo level, and pasture soil sensors — via MQTT and LoRaWAN gateways..

**Author notes:** Send the relevant duration field for goat feed-station waiting time to `index=personal` and review both average and p90 latency instead of relying on single examples.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "goatcare:event", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=goatcare:event earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Goat Feed Station Queue Time** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=goatcare:event`) across the full search range. The `avg, perc90` aggregation groups by `station_id`; change the `by` clause if you want per-device, per-room, or per-user breakdowns instead.

**Fields this search depends on:** `station_id`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=goatcare:event
| search event_type="feed_queue" queue_sec=*
| stats avg(queue_sec) as avg_queue_sec perc90(queue_sec) as p90_queue_sec count as samples by station_id
| sort 0 - avg_queue_sec
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=goatcare:event earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table station_id
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=goatcare:event earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.24.24: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Table Of Average And P90 Goat Feed-Station Waiting Time (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `goatcare:event` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=goatcare:event | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
